mainTopic: Which materials count as a "בגד" for נגעים: the source for including a small שלש על שלש piece of wool or linen, and the exclusion of other fabrics.
overview: The גמרא records a claim (in context, from אביי) that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל hold the same view. The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל learns from the laws of נגעים that every 'garment' in the תורה means wool or linen. רבא disagrees: the two views differ about a שלשה על שלשה (three-by-three handbreadth) piece of other fabrics. Everyone agrees that a שלש על שלש (three-by-three fingerbreadth) piece of wool or linen gets נגעים, and a ברייתא learns this from the extra word 'והבגד'. The גמרא asks why that word does not teach the larger size instead. It concludes that the larger size, useful to rich and poor alike, follows by a קל וחומר from the smaller one, so the פסוק is needed only for the small piece. Next the גמרא asks whether 'והבגד' might include large pieces of other fabrics. It answers that the תורה names wool and linen twice, excluding other fabrics at both sizes, as אביי holds. Finally it turns to ask how this works according to רבא, and that question continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Two sources say the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A claim that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל hold one view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל said the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that two different sources really hold the same view. This line sets up the next steps, which will show what each one said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In context, this is a continuation of אביי's statement. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר was just quoted, saying that among plant fabrics only linen counts. Now the גמרא links his view to a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the study-hall of רבי ישמעאל (a source of ברייתות)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar
and the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael
said one and the same thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from earlier on the דף (the view of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר on linen).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The views of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל are the same.

steps.title: What is the תנא's teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points back to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's known view and asks what the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view is the one we already quoted. What is the teaching of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reminds us that we already know רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view. It then asks what the other source says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To prove the two views match, we need both texts in front of us. One is already known from earlier on the דף, so only the second one needs to be brought.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר — הָא דַּאֲמַרַן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar: that which we said.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל מַאי הִיא?
phrases.english: The Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the text behind the claim in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The wording of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל's teaching.

steps.title: All Torah garments are wool or linen
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from נגעים that every 'garment' in the תורה means wool or linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The תורה uses the word 'garments' in a general way. In one place, the תורה spelled out wool and linen. Just as there it means wool and linen, so too everywhere it means wool and linen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא. It explains the word 'garment' everywhere in the תורה using the one place where the materials are spelled out: the parsha of נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה usually says 'בגד' without saying what it is made of. In ויקרא 13:47 it says 'בגד צמר או בגד פשתים'. The ברייתא uses that one detailed case to define all the others. This matches רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's point that linen is special among plant fabrics.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there... so too (a comparison)

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Since 'garments' are stated in the Torah without detail,
and the verse specified for you in one of them
wool and linen,
just as there it is wool and linen,
so too all garments are wool and linen.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Garments in the תורה are learned from נגעים to be wool or linen only.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, 'בגד' in the תורה means wool or linen.

steps.title: רבא: the two views differ on other fabrics
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the two sources disagree about a three-by-three handbreadth piece of other fabrics.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The difference between them is a piece three by three handbreadths of other fabrics. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds it can become impure. The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל holds it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with the claim that the two sources are identical. He names the exact case where they differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take a piece of other fabric (neither wool nor linen) that measures שלשה על שלשה טפחים. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds it can become טמא. For him, linen is special only because even tiny pieces become impure. The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל limits 'garment' to wool and linen, so other fabrics never count.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
He holds it / he does not hold it

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the grammar! שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה (masculine form) means three handbreadths (טפחים). שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ (feminine form) means three fingerbreadths (אצבעות). The whole sugya depends on telling them apart.

phrases.english: Rava said:
three by three handbreadths in other fabrics
is the difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר — אִית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: For Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds it (that they can become impure).

phrases.aramaic: לְתַנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל — לֵית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: The Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael does not hold it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the claim of step 1 that the two views are identical.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A three-by-three handbreadth piece of other fabrics: impure according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, not impure according to the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: small wool or linen piece gets נגעים
steps.stepSummary: All agree that a three-by-three fingerbreadth piece of wool or linen becomes impure with נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees that a piece three by three fingerbreadths of wool or linen becomes impure with the impurity of נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls out a point everyone agrees on. This sets up a search for the source of that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether we follow אביי or רבא, both sources accept that even a small piece of wool or linen (שלש על שלש אצבעות) is included in the laws of צרעת on garments.

phrases.english: In any case, according to everyone,
three by three fingerbreadths in wool and linen
becomes impure with נגעים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the common ground underneath the dispute of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A three-by-three fingerbreadth piece of wool or linen gets נגעים impurity, according to all.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule about small wool and linen pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the פסוק that teaches the rule just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word 'בגד' suggests a full garment. So the inclusion of a small piece needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that small wool or linen pieces get נגעים.

steps.title: The extra 'ו-ה' in והבגד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the extra word 'והבגד' that a three-by-three fingerbreadth piece is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Garment' teaches me only a full garment. From where do I know a piece three by three fingerbreadths? The verse says 'and the garment'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It shows that the extra letters in 'וְהַבֶּגֶד' widen the law to include small pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בגד' alone would mean a complete garment. The added 'ו' and 'ה' signal an inclusion, a ריבוי. The ברייתא applies that inclusion to the small שלש על שלש piece.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the garment' (the extra letters include more)

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'Garment'
I only know a full garment;
from where do I know three by three fingerbreadths?
The verse says: 'And the garment.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'ו-ה' of 'והבגד' includes the three-by-three fingerbreadth piece.

steps.title: Maybe the extra word includes the bigger size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the extra word may include three handbreadths rather than three fingerbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead that it comes to include a piece three by three handbreadths?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reading. Maybe 'והבגד' includes only the bigger piece, not the tiny one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A larger piece (טפחים) is closer to a real garment, so perhaps the extra word adds only that and leaves out the tiny piece.

phrases.english: But say it comes to include three by three handbreadths?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what the inclusion in step 7 covers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'והבגד' for three fingerbreadths.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The inclusion could cover the larger, more garment-like size instead.

steps.title: The bigger size comes from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The larger size does not need a פסוק, because a קל וחומר from warp and woof threads already teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that not a קל וחומר? Now, if even warp and woof threads become impure, is it necessary to say that three by three handbreadths does?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the bigger piece needs no פסוק. Logic already shows it is impure, so the פסוק must be for the small piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even single warp (שתי) and woof (ערב) threads can get נגעים. A cloth of three handbreadths is far more significant than threads, so it is surely impure. The extra word is therefore free to teach the smaller size.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical 'all the more so' argument
Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.english: Is it not a קל וחומר?
Now, if warp and woof become impure,
is it necessary to say three by three handbreadths?!

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redundancy: the suggested case is already known by logic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra word might include three handbreadths.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three handbreadths is known from a קל וחומר, so the word includes three fingerbreadths.

steps.title: Then the small size also comes from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: If the קל וחומר works, it should teach the small size too, making the פסוק unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let three by three fingerbreadths also be learned through the קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around. The same logic would also cover the small piece, so why would we need the פסוק at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A three-fingerbreadth piece also contains many threads. So it too should be 'all the more so' impure, which would leave 'והבגד' with nothing to teach.

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ נָמֵי לֵיתֵי בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר!
phrases.english: let three by three fingerbreadths also be derived through the קל וחומר!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same קל וחומר would cover the small size, leaving the פסוק with nothing to teach.

steps.title: Useful to rich and poor vs. only to poor
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר works only for a piece useful to everyone, not for one useful only to the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: three by three handbreadths, which is useful to both rich and poor, can be derived through a קל וחומר. Three by three fingerbreadths is useful only to the poor and not to the rich, so it cannot be derived through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the threads argument and gives a new answer to step 8's question. The bigger piece can be learned by a קל וחומר from the smaller piece, because it is useful to more people. The smaller piece cannot be learned that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the גמרא drops the threads argument of step 9. That argument proved too much, as step 10 showed. The new קל וחומר works upward from the small piece: if a שלש על שלש piece, useful only to the poor, is impure, then a שלשה על שלשה piece, useful to rich and poor alike, surely is. The small piece cannot be derived this way, because there is no lesser case to reason from. So 'והבגד' is needed for it.

phrases.english: Rather: three by three handbreadths,
which are fit for both the rich and the poor,
are derived through a קל וחומר.
Three by three fingerbreadths,
are fit only for the poor
and not fit for the rich,
so they are not derived through a קל וחומר.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (usefulness to rich and poor).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר would cover both sizes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three-handbreadth piece is learned by a קל וחומר from the three-fingerbreadth piece, which is useful to fewer people. The three-fingerbreadth piece has no such source, so 'והבגד' must teach it.

steps.title: The small size is included only by the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The small piece is impure only because the פסוק wrote it; logic alone would not include it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that the verse wrote it. Had the verse not written it, we would not learn it through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up. The three-fingerbreadth piece is impure only because of the extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms the ברייתא of step 7. 'והבגד' is needed exactly for the small size, which logic alone could not include.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is that the verse wrote it

steps.whatToRemember: A three-by-three fingerbreadth piece of wool or linen gets נגעים only because of the extra word 'והבגד'. A three-by-three handbreadth piece then follows by a קל וחומר, since it is useful to rich and poor alike, while the small piece is useful only to the poor.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a קל וחומר depends on real significance, here usefulness. A case that matters only to some people needs an explicit פסוק.

phrases.english: The reason is that the verse wrote it;
but had the verse not written it,
we would not derive it through a קל וחומר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the distinction of step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three-by-three fingerbreadth piece of wool or linen is included in נגעים only through the פסוק 'והבגד', not through logic.

steps.title: Maybe the extra word includes a large piece of other fabrics
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the extra word might include a three-by-three handbreadth piece of fabric made from materials other than wool or linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the extra word comes to include a piece of three by three handbreadths in other kinds of garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another possible use for the extra word: it might include three-by-three handbreadth pieces of other fabrics, not just wool and linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps said the extra word teaches about a small piece of wool or linen. Now the גמרא tries a different reading. Maybe the word widens the law to other materials, such as cotton or silk, at the larger size.

keyTerms.meaning: And say instead (a suggested alternative reading)
To include, to add something to the law
Other garments, meaning fabrics that are not wool or linen

phrases.english: But say it comes to include three by three [handbreadths]
phrases.notes: שְׁלֹשָׁה (masculine form) refers to טפחים, handbreadths.

phrases.english: in other garments?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a different thing the extra word could be including.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the extra word is used only for the small piece of wool or linen
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word could just as well widen the law to other materials at the large size.

steps.title: The פסוק limits the law to wool and linen
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק names 'a garment of wool and linen', which shows that only those materials are included and other materials are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'a garment of wool and linen.' A garment of wool and linen, yes. Other things, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The פסוק itself names wool and linen, so other materials cannot be included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק names specific materials, the extra word cannot be used to add a different material. Naming wool and linen works as a limit (מיעוט) on the whole law.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says (introducing a proof from the פסוק)

phrases.english: The verse said: 'A garment of wool and linen.'
A garment of wool and linen, yes,
other things, no.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra word might widen the law to other materials.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק explicitly limits the law to wool and linen.

steps.title: Maybe the limit applies only to the small size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the wool-and-linen limit excludes other materials only at the small size, so a large piece of other material could still become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that when the verse excluded, it excluded only three by three fingerbreadths. A piece of three by three handbreadths, however, does become impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Perhaps the limit only removes small pieces of other materials, while large pieces of other materials remain impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One limiting phrase might only cancel one inclusion. So the גמרא suggests it cancels the small size of other materials, leaving the large size still included.

keyTerms.meaning: Three by three fingerbreadths (a small piece)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the grammar. שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ (feminine) means fingerbreadths, the small size. שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה (masculine) means handbreadths, the large size. The whole step depends on this difference.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא כִּי אִימַּעוּט מִשָּׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: But say that when it excluded, it was from three by three [fingerbreadths],
but three by three [handbreadths] does become impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 14 by narrowing what the limit covers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'wool and linen' fully excludes other materials
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single limiting phrase may exclude other materials only at the small size, not the large size.

steps.title: Two limiting phrases exclude both sizes
steps.stepSummary: The תורה limits the law to wool and linen twice. One limit excludes the small size of other materials, and the other excludes the large size.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two exclusions are written: 'a garment of wool or a garment of linen.' One excludes three by three fingerbreadths, and one excludes three by three handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תורה mentions wool and linen in two places. That gives two limits, one for each size, so other materials are not impure at any size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there are two limiting phrases, each one removes a different size. This means non-wool, non-linen fabric is fully excluded, which matches אביי's view.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this reading (אביי's), garments not made of wool or linen are completely excluded from נגעי בגדים, at both the small size and the large size.

phrases.english: Two exclusions are written:
'A garment of wool or a garment of linen,'
phrases.notes: This is in addition to the phrase 'a garment of wool and linen' already cited.

phrases.english: one to exclude three by three [fingerbreadths],
and one to exclude three by three [handbreadths].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by pointing to a second limiting phrase.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Doubled exclusion: each limiting phrase covers a different size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the small size of other materials is excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sizes of other materials are excluded.

steps.title: Turning to רבא's view of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask about רבא, who says the dispute between רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל is about large pieces of other materials.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, who said the difference between them is three by three handbreadths in other garments: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds it is impure, and the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל does not hold it is impure. That is, three by three handbreadths in other garments...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It restates רבא's view so that it can ask how the extra word is read according to him. The actual question continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13-16 followed אביי, for whom other materials are fully excluded. רבא disagrees: he holds that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does consider large pieces of other materials impure. So the reading just given cannot work for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר according to רבא, and the גמרא needs to explain his source.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disputes with אביי about what the two תנאים argue over
There is a difference between them
He holds it / he does not hold it
The teacher from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the reading of the פסוקים depends on which אמורא's explanation of the מחלוקת we follow.

phrases.english: And according to רבא, who said
three by three [handbreadths] in other garments
is the difference between them,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אִית לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds it [can become impure],

phrases.aramaic: לְתַנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לֵית לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: and the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל does not hold it,
[namely] three by three [handbreadths] in other garments
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד with the actual question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from אביי's reading (steps 13-16) to רבא's competing explanation of the מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the extra word and the limiting phrases are read according to רבא, for whom רבי שמעון בן אלעזר includes large pieces of other materials.
